::: {#sol-only-if}

"If I go to class, then I am healthy."

The sentence says that going to class requires being healthy,
so whenever I go to class, I am healthy.
It does not say "if I am healthy, then I go to class";
that is its converse (@def-converse),
and a healthy person may still skip class.

In general, "$P$ only if $Q$" means $P \Rightarrow Q$.

:::
